After `go env -w CGO_ENABLED=1`, `go env CGO_ENABLED` still prints 0 (Go warns that the OS environment wins); under env -i it prints 1, and after `go env -u` it prints 0 (go.env), as docs/kubernetes.md says. The documented boundary, a go/build reader under env -i, gets cgo on and still passes (supervise ok 5.170s, gcc present). --check-config refuses pod.env CGO_ENABLED "1" and "0" with exit 1: `runtime.kubernetes.pod.env sets CGO_ENABLED, which the worker image sets (packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile ENV)`. proof.negativeControl: A `legion` built from main 135d22e0 prints `Config OK: project=WIDGETS` (exit 0) for the same file with pod.env CGO_ENABLED that this head refuses. In the head image, `go env -w CGO_ENABLED=1` under env -i turns cgo on (1), so the 0 the scrubbed environment reads comes from the go.env default, not from cgo being unavailable.

observations: Coverage: the image probe and the build's `gcc --version` step catch a dropped gcc (shown by the hidden-gcc probe run). TestImageEnvIsWhatTheWorkerImageSets catches a dropped ENV. Nothing but a live run catches a dropped /opt/go/go.env line, as the PR body's risk line already says. If that line is lost, only scrubbed environments (the eval kernel) get cgo on, and with gcc present those builds still succeed, linked dynamically. Not a defect at this head, so no red test.

Not reproduced: a real Sandbox issue pod and Oh My Pi's real eval kernel on the new image. A python3 subprocess with the kernel's allowlist (read from this tester's own live eval kernel, which carries no image ENV) stands in for the kernel; the production check covers the real pod.

The tester's issue pod mounts /legion over 9p under gVisor, and building and running a binary from $TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/tmp works there (exec-ok), so the emptyDir in the Job does not hide an exec restriction a role's TMPDIR would have.
